head: 7bc5ef2a1057c5571acab8d9e1e1a8bbf879cf86
reasons: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py's _part_targets git-verb branch (`elif headl == "git" and len(words) >= 2: sub = words[1].lower()`) still reads the subcommand from the fixed position words[1] with no flag-skipping, unlike the cp/mv/rm/tee branches which run _nonflag first. Traced `git -c core.fileMode=false rm CLAUDE.md` by hand: words=['git','-c','core.fileMode=false','rm','CLAUDE.md']; sub becomes '-c', matches none of checkout/restore/rm/mv/apply, so _part_targets yields no candidate and decide() allows a command that genuinely deletes the guardrail file. No token is non-literal, so the fail-closed rule never fires. plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's allow-list already permits bare Bash(git *), so this is reachable in CI, not just by hand.

_inner_shell_command (`if len(words) >= 3 and (words[0].lower(), words[1].lower()) in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS: return words[2]`) still only recognises the exact adjacent pair. Traced `bash --norc -c 'echo x > CLAUDE.md'`: words=['bash','--norc','-c',...]; ('bash','--norc') is not in _INNER_SHELL_PAIRS, so the quoted inner command is never recursed into; the '>' sits inside the single-quoted outer token so it is correctly treated as literal text at the outer level, not a redirection operator; shell_write_targets returns [] and decide() allows a command that writes the guardrail file via an inner shell.

Both gaps are exactly the class of vulnerability intent.md and spec.md's Design section exist to close (git rm/restore/checkout/apply and bash -c/sh -c recursion are both named as covered idioms with no flag-position qualification); they are not part of plan.md's named residual (unlisted wrappers, pathspec-less git verbs, variable-built paths) -- a leading flag on an already-recognised verb or wrapper is a different, narrower shape that was missed, not weighed and accepted.

No test in tests/test_hooks.py exercises a git invocation with a global option before the subcommand, or an inner-shell call with a flag between the interpreter name and its -c/-Command token: the existing 'git -c user.name=x commit -m y' case belongs to test_plan_sync_detects_commit_in_any_position (a different hook), and test_shell_write_targets_sees_through_wrappers_and_inner_shells only exercises the bare adjacent pairs. The tests therefore pass with both bugs present -- they do not reproduce either bypass.

This is the second review of this exact pair of bugs: the prior HEAD's escalation (08f5e65) already found and described both precisely; fix-requests.json for this round shows empty requests/not_applied, and verifier.md scopes itself explicitly to re-verifying only the unrelated git -C chain-leak fix (commit 3a90bd0), not these two. The devil's-advocate/panel round (commit 7bc5ef2, the only new commit since 08f5e65) upheld 'escalate' as 'park' rather than closing it; no source file changed in that commit. Independently re-tracing both repros against plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py at this HEAD confirms they are unchanged and the bugs are still live.

Blast radius: this is the change's own security control (risk_list item 'auth', status.yaml risk_accepted: [auth]) and the file registered on every Bash/PowerShell call in every phase and in CI (plugin/hooks/hooks.json); a gap in the authorization gate itself, reachable through an already allow-listed program (git) with no non-literal token to trip the fail-closed rule, is the exact failure mode intent.md was opened to close, not a cosmetic nit.
classification_reasons: Security/authorization control (risk_list item 'auth'), explicitly risk-accepted by the owner, not a tight closed spec: two concrete bypasses remain open against spec.md's own Design claims.
Blast radius is the guardrail-protection mechanism itself, registered on every Bash/PowerShell tool call across every phase, in CI and by hand -- not a small or isolated surface.

The existing and newly-added tests do not cover the git-verb-flag-position or inner-shell-flag-position cases, so the code's current behavior (allow when it should deny) is not caught by any test in the diff.
attempted: Intent: compared the artifact against intent.md's proposed outcome ('no instance of this authz weakness remains'); it does not hold yet -- two concrete, literal-command bypasses of the new hook remain, in the same class the intent names.

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md Design's write-idiom list and plan.md's Order of work and Options-not-taken/Risks sections; the git-verb and inner-shell-recursion idioms are claimed unqualified by flag position, but the implementation reads a fixed word index for both, which the spec text does not call out as a limitation.

Proof: read evidence/verifier.md (scope explicitly limited to the git -C chain-leak fix, commit 3a90bd0, confirmed sound) and evidence/fix-requests.json (empty requests/not_applied for this round); neither closes or claims to close the two open bugs. Did not cite or rely on any claude-*.json/run-*.json runner record as evidence for or against the diff.

Blast radius: shell_guard.py is registered on every Bash/PowerShell call (hooks.json), touches the risk_list 'auth' item, and both bypasses are reachable through bare `Bash(git *)` already on plugin/ci/settings.ci.json's allow-list -- not confined to an unusual or already-mitigated path.

Policies: security-baseline rule 1 (authorization must not depend on which route reaches the target) is the rule this whole change exists to satisfy; the two bugs are instances of exactly that failure mode surviving inside the fix itself.

Tests: read tests/test_hooks.py's shell_guard tests (wrapper/inner-shell and git coverage) directly; confirmed by grep that no test passes a flagged git invocation (`git -c ...`) or a flagged inner-shell wrapper (`bash --norc -c ...`) through shell_guard -- the tests would stay green with either bug present, satisfying the 'tests pass with the bug present' trigger.

Cross-checked this verdict is independent of the gate's own deterministic checks and of the panel's prior verdict (evidence/decisions-c.json, which reached the same conclusion through a different review this reviewer did not read as authority -- re-traced both repros from the source directly rather than citing the panel's record as the reason).
